definitionEn: A young human who has not yet reached adulthood.
example: Every child deserves a safe place to learn and play.

definitionEn: A very young child who has only recently started walking.
example: The toddler laughed loudly when the puppy licked his face.

definitionEn: A person aged between thirteen and nineteen years old.
example: Many teenagers spend hours on their phones after school.

definitionEn: The period of a person's life when they are a child.
example: Her happiest memories are of summers spent at her grandmother's house during childhood.

definitionEn: An outdoor area with equipment where children play at school or in a park.
example: The children ran straight to the playground as soon as the bell rang.

definitionEn: Tasks that pupils are given by teachers to complete at home.
example: She finished her maths homework before dinner and then watched television.

definitionEn: A place where very young children are cared for while parents work.
example: My son started at the nursery when he was just two years old.

definitionEn: A sudden outburst of anger, often shown by a young child.
example: The little boy threw a tantrum because he could not have sweets.

definitionEn: Eager to learn or know more about something.
example: Young children are naturally curious and ask questions about everything.

definitionEn: Willing to do what you are told by parents or teachers.
example: The obedient child put away his toys without being asked twice.

definitionEn: Behaving badly, especially in a playful way that breaks small rules.
example: The naughty puppy chewed my shoes while I was in the kitchen.

definitionEn: Kind, calm, and careful in the way you treat people.
example: The nurse was gentle with the frightened little girl during the check-up.

definitionEn: A brother or sister.
example: Each sibling in our family has a different personality and interests.

definitionEn: An object designed for children to play with.
example: The child's favourite toy was a battered teddy bear with one eye.

definitionEn: The time when a person usually goes to bed.
example: Bedtime is at eight o'clock on school nights in our house.

definitionEn: To care for and encourage a child's growth and development.
example: Good teachers nurture curiosity by encouraging students to ask questions.

definitionEn: To watch over and direct someone's activities to make sure they are safe.
example: Parents should supervise young children when they swim in the sea.

definitionEn: A time by which a young person must be home at night.
example: My parents set a curfew of ten o'clock on weekday nights.

definitionEn: An adult legally responsible for caring for a child whose parents cannot.
example: The court appointed her aunt as the child's legal guardian.

definitionEn: To tell someone a private or personal thought in confidence.
example: Many teenagers confide in a close friend rather than their parents.

definitionEn: Easily upset or hurt by criticism or by other people's words.
example: Some children are very sensitive to criticism, even when it is gentle.

definitionEn: Acting quickly on feelings without thinking carefully about the results.
example: The impulsive boy jumped into the pool before anyone could stop him.

definitionEn: Refusing to change your opinion or behaviour, even when others ask you to.
example: The stubborn toddler refused to eat anything except bananas.

definitionEn: Giving encouragement and help to someone in need.
example: Supportive parents praise effort, not just results, when children try hard.

definitionEn: A private teacher who gives extra lessons to a pupil.
example: She hired a tutor to help her son prepare for the entrance exam.

definitionEn: A regular meeting where young children play together with adults supervising.
example: My daughter made her first friends at a local playgroup.

definitionEn: A strong emotional connection between people, such as parent and child.
example: The bond between a baby and its mother forms very early in life.

definitionEn: A close relationship between people who like and trust each other.
example: A lasting friendship helps children feel secure during difficult times.

definitionEn: The stage when a child's body begins to develop into an adult body.
example: Puberty can bring big changes in mood, appearance, and friendships.

definitionEn: A person of the same age or status as another person.
example: Teenagers often value their peers' opinions more than their parents' advice.

definitionEn: Relying on someone else for money, support, or care.
example: Young children are completely dependent on adults for food and shelter.

definitionEn: The ability to act and make decisions without relying on others.
example: Learning independence early helps children become confident adults.

definitionEn: An occasion when a child spends the night at a friend's house.
example: Her daughter begged to go to a sleepover at her best friend's house.

definitionEn: Feeling sad because you are away from home and miss your family.
example: The homesick student called his mother every night during his first term.

definitionEn: Having a strong desire to achieve success or reach high goals.
example: Ambitious students often set themselves demanding targets for each school year.

definitionEn: Thoughtful about other people's feelings and needs.
example: A considerate child remembers to say thank you after every meal.

definitionEn: Relating to the mental processes of thinking, learning, and remembering.
example: Reading aloud supports cognitive growth in children during the early school years.

definitionEn: The process of growing up physically, emotionally, or intellectually.
example: Emotional maturation often lags behind physical growth during the early teens.

definitionEn: Relating to the stages by which a person grows and changes.
example: Paediatricians monitor developmental progress at every routine check-up.

definitionEn: A person's natural way of thinking, feeling, and reacting to things.
example: Some babies have a calm temperament, while others cry at every noise.

definitionEn: A feeling of restraint that stops a person from acting freely or spontaneously.
example: Shyness can create inhibition that stops children from speaking in class.

definitionEn: Easily influenced by the ideas or behaviour of others.
example: Young children are highly impressionable and copy the adults around them.

definitionEn: Showing skills or maturity at an earlier age than is usual.
example: The precocious girl could already read novels at the age of five.

definitionEn: Relating to punishment or rules used to control behaviour.
example: The school introduced new disciplinary rules after several fights in the playground.

definitionEn: Allowing someone to have or do what they want, often too easily.
example: Indulgent grandparents often spoil children with sweets and expensive toys.

definitionEn: Protecting someone so much that they cannot become independent.
example: Overprotective parents may prevent children from taking healthy risks.

definitionEn: Appearing calm and unconcerned, even when a situation is serious.
example: The teenager was nonchalant about failing the test and shrugged it off.

definitionEn: Refusal to obey rules, orders, or instructions from those in authority.
example: Repeated disobedience led to the boy being moved to another class.

definitionEn: A formal expression of disapproval given to someone who has done wrong.
example: The head teacher gave the pupil a stern reprimand for bullying.

definitionEn: A young person who is developing from a child into an adult.
example: Adolescent brains are still developing, which affects decision making.

meaningVi: cạnh tranh giữa anh chị em
definitionEn: Competition and jealousy between brothers and sisters for attention.
example: Sibling rivalry often eases once children grow older and more independent.

definitionEn: Able to understand and share the feelings of another person.
example: An empathetic teacher notices when a student is feeling sad or anxious.

definitionEn: Selfless concern for the wellbeing of others.
example: Children can learn altruism by helping classmates and volunteering in their community.

definitionEn: Sympathy and a strong desire to relieve another's suffering.
example: She showed great compassion when her classmate lost a parent.

definitionEn: A person's natural mood, character, or tendency to behave in a particular way.
example: The child has a cheerful disposition that lifts everyone around her.

definitionEn: Difficult circumstances or misfortune that challenge a person.
example: Children who overcome adversity often develop remarkable inner strength.

definitionEn: The ability to keep going through a difficult or tiring experience.
example: Long-distance running builds endurance and patience in young athletes.

definitionEn: The state of being open to harm, criticism, or emotional hurt.
example: Adolescents show great vulnerability to peer rejection and online bullying.

definitionEn: Quiet and reserved, avoiding contact with other people.
example: The withdrawn boy sat alone at lunch and rarely spoke in class.

definitionEn: Showing a strong interest in learning about things.
example: An inquisitive child asks questions about how everything works.

definitionEn: A natural ability or talent for learning a particular skill.
example: She showed a strong aptitude for mathematics from a very early age.

meaningVi: sự dạy dỗ, sự giám hộ
definitionEn: Guidance, instruction, or protection given by a teacher or guardian.
example: Under the tutelage of an experienced coach, the young swimmer improved quickly.

meaningVi: hành vi phạm pháp thanh thiếu niên
definitionEn: Antisocial or illegal behaviour, especially by young people.
example: Researchers link family neglect with a higher risk of juvenile delinquency.

definitionEn: The practice of staying away from school without permission.
example: Persistent truancy can cause serious gaps in a student's education.

definitionEn: The ability to manage one's own emotions, behaviour, and impulses.
example: Self-regulation skills help children wait their turn and handle frustration.

definitionEn: The act of copying the speech, movements, or behaviour of others.
example: Young children learn language partly through mimicry of their parents.

meaningVi: tự cho mình là trung tâm
definitionEn: Focused on one's own needs and perspective, without considering others.
example: Toddlers are naturally egocentric and find it hard to share.

definitionEn: Having mixed or conflicting feelings about someone or something.
example: Many teenagers feel ambivalent about moving to a new school.

definitionEn: Bitter anger at being treated unfairly or given less than others.
example: Favouritism among siblings often breeds resentment that lasts for years.

definitionEn: Belonging naturally to something; coming from within rather than from outside.
example: Intrinsic motivation makes children keep learning for the joy of it.

definitionEn: Careful and thorough in doing one's work or duties.
example: The conscientious pupil always checks her homework twice before submitting it.

definitionEn: Enjoying the company of others and seeking social contact.
example: My gregarious nephew makes friends with everyone at the playground.

definitionEn: Comfort received after a loss or disappointment.
example: Her pet rabbit provided solace during the difficult months after the move.

definitionEn: Unwilling to speak openly about feelings or thoughts.
example: The reticent girl rarely shared her feelings with her teachers.

definitionEn: The method and practice of teaching, especially the theory behind it.
example: Modern pedagogy emphasises active learning over memorising facts.

definitionEn: Just beginning to develop or show signs of growth.
example: The child showed a nascent talent for drawing at only three years old.

definitionEn: Unusually early development of mental or physical abilities in a child.
example: Her precocity surprised teachers, who had never met such an advanced reader.

definitionEn: Childishly silly or immature, especially in behaviour that should be outgrown.
example: His puerile jokes embarrassed everyone at the otherwise serious meeting.

definitionEn: Relating to young people, or characteristic of immaturity.
example: Juvenile offenders are often placed in separate facilities from adult prisoners.

definitionEn: Relating to infants, or showing childish immaturity in an adult.
example: His infantile sulking during the game annoyed his teammates.

definitionEn: Relating to or showing the duty and respect expected of a son or daughter.
example: She showed filial devotion by caring for her father through his illness.

definitionEn: Relating to a father, or the protective care of a father.
example: His paternal instincts made him protective of his younger brother.

definitionEn: Relating to a mother, or the protective care of a mother.
example: Maternal love shapes a child's sense of security in the earliest years.

definitionEn: Kind, friendly, and warmly helpful, like a favourite uncle.
example: The avuncular teacher always had a kind word for anxious pupils.

definitionEn: Having or showing keen judgement and good sense.
example: The sagacious old headmaster knew exactly how to calm a quarrel.

definitionEn: Acting quickly and rashly without considering the consequences.
example: The impetuous boy ran into the road without looking for traffic.

definitionEn: Eager to argue or fight; aggressively defiant.
example: The truculent teenager refused every suggestion his parents offered.

definitionEn: Childishly bad-tempered or sulky about small matters.
example: The petulant toddler stamped his feet when his juice was finished.

definitionEn: Difficult to control, and inclined to behave badly or unpredictably.
example: The wayward son ignored his father's advice and left school early.

definitionEn: Too firmly fixed in bad habits to be corrected or reformed.
example: The incorrigible prankster never stopped playing tricks on his classmates.

definitionEn: Quiet and easy to control or teach.
example: The docile puppy followed the children around the garden all afternoon.

definitionEn: Easily shaped or influenced, especially in character or opinion.
example: Young minds are pliable and can be shaped by early experiences.

definitionEn: Having a strong influence on the development of character during early years.
example: Her formative years in the countryside shaped her love of nature.

definitionEn: The process of teaching someone to accept a set of beliefs without question.
example: Critics warn that rigid schooling can become indoctrination rather than education.

definitionEn: Intended to teach a lesson, often in a preachy or overly instructive way.
example: The picture book is too didactic and lectures children on every page.

definitionEn: Providing emotional release and relief through expressing strong feelings.
example: Writing in a diary was cathartic for the teenager after the family argument.

definitionEn: The examination of one's own thoughts and feelings.
example: Adolescence often brings deep introspection about identity and purpose.

definitionEn: A feeling of listlessness and dissatisfaction caused by boredom.
example: Some students feel ennui during long lessons that offer no challenge.

definitionEn: Showing care and concern for someone's wellbeing.
example: The solicitous nurse checked on the sick child every hour.

definitionEn: Optimistic and cheerful, especially in difficult circumstances.
example: Despite the setbacks, the coach remained sanguine about the team's chances.

definitionEn: Modest or shy, lacking confidence in oneself.
example: The diffident boy hesitated before raising his hand in class.

definitionEn: Cheerful and full of energy and enthusiasm.
example: The ebullient children burst into the classroom after the holiday.

definitionEn: Irritable and quarrelsome, especially when tired or bored.
example: The fractious toddlers grew tired and began to fight over toys.

definitionEn: Silent and bad-tempered, showing resentment through a gloomy expression.
example: The sullen teenager said nothing during the entire family dinner.

definitionEn: Sad, bad-tempered, and gloomy, often withdrawing from others.
example: The morose boy stayed in his room for days after losing the match.

definitionEn: Lacking energy, enthusiasm, or the will to act.
example: The lethargic child slept late and refused to join the morning exercises.

definitionEn: A rule or principle intended to guide behaviour or conduct.
example: Her grandmother's precept was always to treat others with respect.

definitionEn: A person's children or descendants.
example: The king's progeny were educated abroad to prepare them for rule.

definitionEn: A young member of a noble or wealthy family.
example: The scion of the merchant family was sent to study in London.

definitionEn: The relationship between people who share a common ancestor.
example: Consanguinity between the two families was revealed through old church records.

definitionEn: A person or thing that is new and inexperienced in a particular field.
example: The fledgling designer won her first major commission at twenty-two.

definitionEn: A beginner who has just started learning a skill or activity.
example: The neophyte teacher struggled with discipline during her first month.

definitionEn: A child whose parents have died.
example: The charity supports orphan children with food, schooling, and medical care.

definitionEn: Young, inexperienced, and naive.
example: The callow youth believed everything his friends told him.

definitionEn: Socially awkward and lacking grace or tact.
example: The gauche teenager knocked over a glass at the formal dinner.

definitionEn: Difficult to control and disorderly in behaviour.
example: The unruly class ignored the substitute teacher completely.

definitionEn: Loud, harsh, and noisy in a rowdy way.
example: The raucous children shouted and laughed all the way down the corridor.

definitionEn: Bad-tempered and quarrelsome, especially in an old or contrary way.
example: The cantankerous old man complained about the children playing outside.

definitionEn: Noisy and difficult to control, refusing to obey.
example: The obstreperous pupils refused to sit down until the bell rang.

definitionEn: Causing annoyance or irritation, often without good reason.
example: The vexatious parent sent a stream of complaints about every small matter.
